hook: SCP-143 is a valley planted with three hundred trees that look like Japanese cherry blossoms, except that the petals are glassy, translucent and sharp enough to slice skin. It is a short file, most of it a materials report, so read slowly. The safety rules in the procedures are worth remembering by the time you reach the last paragraph.
whyItMatters:
The appeal here is an image more than a plot: a beautiful seasonal scene rebuilt as a hazard, with wood and petals harder than most natural or manufactured materials yet still as pliable as ordinary wood. The addendum ties the grove to a lineage of swordsmiths in Nara who claim descent from a legendary blademaker named Amakuni, which grounds the anomaly in craft rather than monsters.

It also shows how much a single closing note can do. A file that reads like an engineering datasheet ends on a few plain lines from someone on site, and those lines reframe everything above them.
thingsToNotice:
The procedures ask staff not to stand under the trees without protective gear and to clear the area whenever shedding starts, and they list the petals' twice-yearly fall almost as a convenience for harvesting armor and weapon material. Document 143-A then spends that warning: three staff were picking up petals from the day before when a sudden gust stripped more from the branches and blew them through the grove, and the wind kept up all day. The writer simply notes that cleanup has to wait until the wind drops and the remains can be collected.

The addendum's quieter detail is political, since the original grove is still in Japan, owned and kept secret by the government, tended by the same family, and its products never leave the country.
